question: Three primes, \(p,\) \(q\) and \(r,\) satisfy \(p+q=r\) and \(1\lt p\lt q.\) Then \(p\) equals
solution: The only even prime is \(2\), because every larger even number has \(2\) as a factor besides \(1\) and itself. If \(p>2\), then \(q>p\) makes both primes odd. Their sum \(r=p+q\) would then be even and greater than \(2\), contradicting that \(r\) is prime. Therefore \(p=2\). These conditions are possible, as \(2+3=5\). The answer is \(\boxed{2}\), choice A.
